correctness.rationale: Write s=H restricted to [0,1), π for fractional part, and G(t)={1111t}. Integer gains give H=sπ and G=πs pointwise, including all discontinuities (thus the globally typed relation is πH=Gπ). The identity H^n=sG^(n−1)π gives the unique lift of each G^n-fixed point, hence the stated census and zeta. Invariance makes s_* and π_* inverse on invariant probabilities; the two factor maps preserve ergodicity and give entropy equality by monotonicity in both directions, not by asserting pointwise conjugacy. Lebesgue on the circle is the exact uniform 1111-symbol shift, and s pushes it to an absolutely continuous law by affine change of variables; any absolutely continuous invariant law projects to an absolutely continuous invariant circle law, which is unique by exactness. Birkhoff applied to s composed with a countable convergence-determining set of bounded continuous tests gives physicality. The branch formula gives nonuniform density (near zero only the first affine interval contributes); the total variation is 1111+999+99+9, so coupling a uniform t with the grid point immediately to its left establishes the W₁ bound. For the covariance I also obtained P( {at}−1/2 )=({at}−1/2)/1111 for the Lebesgue transfer operator P of G when gcd(a,1111)=1: the residues a j modulo 1111 permute the branches. This gives the all-lag scaling directly. The sawtooth pair integral from matching Fourier harmonics gives Var=(4+2(3/10+2/100+1/1000))/12=2321/6000; geometric summation gives the normalized spectrum in the stated convention. The frozen checker was inspected, not executed; analytic identities establish the universal claims.
residual_risks: Only exact real arithmetic with the specified half-open convention is verified; this is not a finite-precision implementation result or a security claim.

The factorization determines all invariant laws and all fixed-point counts rather than just the instability of a typical orbit. The exact variance, density and all-lag spectrum give a benchmark for a concrete nonuniform observable: a simple geometric law for memory despite the nonuniform one-time distribution. They can be used to distinguish exact dynamics from numerical artifacts without treating them as evidence about security.
